precepts.text: Evil communication will corrupt good manners. What you digest in your vision and your hearing will change the way you think.
precepts.point: Exercise these senses in what we watch, like Bishop pulled in Job 31, our hearing, what we ingest, we listen to. Evil communication will corrupt good manners. What you digest in your vision and your hearing will change the way you think. We have to exercise those physical senses so we can tap into the spiritual senses that we have, and that's intuition. Well, we gonna get to that. I don't want to talk about it too much, because I don't want to jump the gun. Okay. The tongue. Let's go to the book of Job 33. The tongue, I'm going to splice that with speech. All right. So I can kind of shorten this. 33, verse 1.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
Moses commanded: “thou shalt read this law before all Israel in their hearing.” In their hearing. “Gather the people together, men, and women, and children, and thy stranger that is within thy gates, that they may hear, and that they may learn, and fear the Lord your God, and observe to do all the words of this law”. Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God: in hearing we process what we heard, learn from it, and apply it to our life.

So we have to exercise these senses: in what we watch, as Job 31 was pulled up, and in our hearing, what we ingest and listen to. “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” What you digest in your vision and your hearing will change the way you think.

That is why the law is read in the hearing of the whole house, even “their children, which have not known any thing”, so that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord. If the ear is filled with the law, it forms the mind in the law; if it is filled with evil communications, it corrupts the manners.

We exercise the physical senses, what we see and what we hear, so we can tap into the spiritual senses we have. Going from milk to meat means training the ear on the word of God and guarding it from everything that would corrupt it.

precepts.text: I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: that is the dying daily. Lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway. Paul knew he would drift if he did not die daily and give life to the spiritual man daily.
precepts.point: I die daily. Paul is talking about that same daily: you starve the carnal man and feed the spiritual man.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
Christ said, “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.” There is that daily again. Paul says it of himself: “I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.” How do you do it? By feeding. You deny the carnal man and feed the spiritual man. Not that you stop eating; you starve the carnal and feed the spiritual.

Paul shows it in chapter 9: “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection”. That is the dying daily. “lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway”. Paul preached to others, but he knew he would drift if he did not die daily and give life to the spiritual man daily as well.

Romans says the same: “if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live.” You cannot do that without constant connection to the scriptures. Many say they are battling depression or sin, but they do not open their Bible every day; they are not battling anything. When somebody with good works and a good reputation moves to the left or the right, it is because they stopped feeding themselves daily. That is scary; we all have to check ourselves.

There is no excuse anymore: you have a Bible with you all the time, on your phone. The pattern runs through the whole book: daily bread, daily mercy, take up your cross daily, daily death, daily renewal. “though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day”. The outward man dies; the inward man must be fed. That is daily bread for a dying man.

precepts.text: Now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept. Every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming. The same promise stands for us if we believe and keep the commandments in the faith of Christ.
precepts.point: The feast of firstfruits: count seven sabbaths complete from the wave offering, and number fifty days. Seven sabbaths again, complete.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
The two wave loaves of Leviticus 23:17 “are the firstfruits unto the Lord.” Paul shows who the firstfruits are: “But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.” Christ is the firstfruits.

“For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.” Then the order is set: “But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming.”

The same promise stands for us if we believe and keep the commandments in the faith of Christ: first Christ was raised, and afterward we that are his are raised at his coming.

Like the sabbath, the passover and the feast of unleavened bread before it, the feast of firstfruits is a representation of Christ. All seven of the high holy days read in Leviticus 23 represent Jesus Christ, and seven sabbaths counted “complete” to the fifty days points to completion in him.

precepts.text: Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go: lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul. The bitter brother is like that dangerous brush; there could be a viper in there. Get too close and the bitter spirit gets on you.
precepts.point: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners. Bitterness spreads like leaven through words: the yeast makes the thing rise, and the angry influence spreads to others through words and attitude.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
“evil communications corrupt good manners.” Bitterness spreads like leaven through words: the yeast makes things rise, and that is what bitterness does. The root of bitterness corrupts your spirit and messes with your attitude, and that angry influence spreads to others through words and through attitude.

So Proverbs warns: “Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go”. You see that brother is bitter; he is like that dangerous overgrown brush. There could be a viper in there, anything on the other side of that bush. Move.

“Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.” Now that bitter brother has put the bitter spirit on you. You got bit, like Bird Box, and now you are looking dumb. That is the snare right there.

That is why the scripture says be not deceived. Keeping company with the bitter brother is how the leaven gets into you. His evil communications will corrupt your good manners, and his offenses will reach others, starting with the first offense, the one in your own house.

precepts.text: The second man is the Lord from heaven. The Lord from heaven is Christ: that is the Almighty word that leaped off his throne and came down in Exodus.
precepts.point: Pharaoh's chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red Sea. Who did that? The Lord. Thy right hand, O Lord, hath dashed in pieces the enemy. This is the wars of the Lord we are reading about: when the Lord fought against the Egyptians, drowned them in the Red Sea, and brought plagues upon them.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
Who is the Almighty word that leaped down off his throne? “The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven.” The Lord from heaven is Christ. He is the one who came down and killed the Egyptians in Exodus, and that is why Moses says the Lord is a man of war.

Paul says the same thing about the wilderness: our fathers “drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” And Exodus 13:21: “the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire”. That pillar of cloud was a chariot, and the Lord inside it was Christ. Who was following us in the wilderness? Christ. Who killed the Egyptians? Christ.

So when Exodus 15:3 says “the Lord is his name”, it is speaking of the anointed. He smote the Egyptians, and the same way he is going to come back in the future and smite spiritual Egypt, the land we are living in today.

precepts.text: Every one that was in distress, in debt, and discontented gathered themselves unto David, and he became a captain over them, about four hundred men. The beginning of IUIC was men with problems and issues, not the full package, taken in and built with structure and discipline, as the women are built through Ladies in Waiting, Titus 2, and Daughters of Sarah. 2 Samuel 17:8: thy father and his men be mighty men, chafed in their minds as a bear robbed of her whelps. Not mighty at first; David put in the work, as the leadership put work in us.
precepts.point: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners. Evil communications come to men and women, and when they come you shut them down and do not entertain them, as the captain was drilling, or you end up caught in foolishness. A father who came up through this will make sure his sons learn that discipline and are not given feminine softness, so that when he grows up he can deal with a woman properly. That is not abuse.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders & Fathers: the Children Are Listening

precepts.why:
“And every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves unto him; and he became a captain over them: and there were with him about four hundred men.”

The men who gathered to David were not the full package. They were in distress, in debt and discontented: men with problems and issues. David took them in and became a captain over them. That was the beginning of IUIC too: men with problems and issues, taken in and built with structure and discipline. The women are built the same way, through Ladies in Waiting, Titus 2 and Daughters of Sarah.

Later those same men are spoken of differently. In 2 Samuel 17:8 Hushai says to Absalom, “thou knowest thy father and his men, that they be mighty men, and they be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field.” They were not mighty at first. David put in the work, the same way the leadership put the work in us.

That is why it sits with “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” Everyone comes in with negative impulses, and we expect it. Hard times create warriors against sinful impulses, and the men are the vanguards of righteousness, to ward off any semblance of sin. When evil communications come to men and women, you shut them down and do not entertain them. The ones who come in get tried and watched, and the demons get exercised out of them through the congregation, the brothers and sisters that are watching them. If you really want to get yourself right, you will thank them for the wounds of a friend rather than the kisses of an enemy. But if you refuse to change, you have to go, because we cannot let a bad example destroy the rest of the flock.

precepts.text: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming.
precepts.point: As concerning the gospel they are enemies for your sakes, but as touching the election they are beloved for the fathers' sakes. As ye in times past had not believed God but now have obtained mercy through their unbelief, so they through your mercy may obtain mercy. God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all: all Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
“For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy”. Who is the firstfruit? Paul answers it in Corinthians: “But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming.”

Christ is the firstfruits. It starts with Christ, because he is our creator, the rock that begat us, and then it goes to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as well. “Afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming” means the elect.

And the lump is Israel. If the firstfruit is holy, the lump is also holy: because Christ is holy, the people that come after him in his order are holy too.

So Romans 11 opens by tying Israel to Christ. The same holy firstfruit stands at the head of the whole lump, and that is why God has not cast away his people. Both kingdoms, the branches that fell and the branches grafted back in, belong to that holy lump that follows Christ.

precepts.text: If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily.
precepts.point: Deny yourself, take up your cross daily, and follow Christ.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
“I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.” What did Paul do? He died daily. Paul put himself out there, did the work, and killed the old man daily. Brothers, that is your job too: you have to kill that old man daily.

But how do you do that? Did Paul just sit on his ass? Christ makes it very clear: “And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.” That is how he dies daily: he denies himself, and he takes up his cross.

We are all commanded to take up our cross and die daily. To take up your cross is to accept your death when it comes. Kill the old man. And if they take you out, take your death: we will be back.

It is a war. You have to execute the man in you to be able to see the conniving, deceitful, envious, jealous, hateful, murderous spirit of these other nations against our people. You have to remove that old man to have a sense of clarity. Twelve tribes, twelve trials.

precepts.text: All flesh is not the same flesh; there is flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds, so fish is meat.
precepts.point: Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
Fish is meat. “All flesh is not the same flesh: but there is one kind of flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, and another of birds.” The flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are not the same flesh, but they are all flesh. “God giveth it a body as it hath pleased him, and to every seed his own body.”

So when the Most High says “Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you”, fish is included as meat, and it is under the same dietary law that sanctifies what may be eaten.

precepts.text: There are celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial; the Most High has an angelic celestial body.
precepts.point: Christ was not reincarnated when he came in the flesh. He took not on him the nature of angels, but the seed of Abraham, made like unto his brethren, born a man so that he could die for the nation of Israel, for an angel cannot die.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
“All flesh is not the same flesh: but there is one kind of flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, and another of birds. There are also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another.”

God is a Spirit, but He has a body: a celestial, angelic body, not flesh of this earth. That is how the angel of the Lord could appear to Moses in a flame of fire out of the midst of the bush, and how man could be made in His image.

precepts.text: There are celestial bodies and bodies terrestrial; our earthly bodies are made of the ground, but the angels have celestial bodies, which is why they can appear, disappear, and stand all around us right now listening and recording without us knowing.
precepts.point: Gideon brings a kid and unleavened cakes, and the angel touches the flesh and the cakes with the end of his staff; fire rises up out of the rock and consumes them, and the angel departs out of his sight, gone just like that. No lighter fluid existed on the earth; the angel made fire come out of the rock, because the angels are made out of that fire.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
The angel touched the flesh and the unleavened cakes with the end of his staff, “and there rose up fire out of the rock”, and then he “departed out of his sight”, gone just like that. No lighter fluid existed on the earth; the angel made fire come out of the rock, because the angels are made out of that fire.

“There are also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another.” Our earthly bodies are made of the ground, terrestrial. The angels have celestial bodies, which is why they can appear, disappear, bring fire out of a rock, and stand all around us right now listening and recording without us knowing.

precepts.text: Evil communications corrupt good manners; what is played into the ears works on the spirit.
precepts.point: The songs we make and listen to, now that we know the truth, should be spiritual songs; the psalms were the jams of that day, and every one of them is deep, teaching who the daughter of Babylon is, the crafty counsel taken against us, and that the law was given to Israel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
“Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” What is played into the ears works on the spirit.

If a spiritual song can heal, so that Saul “shalt be well” when the harp is played, think what an evil song can do to a good spirit. Be mindful when it comes to music.

precepts.text: Christ is risen as the firstfruits; God has put all things under his feet, subjecting the whole earth and spiritual realm to the Son.
precepts.point: Christ had to be made lower than the angels so that he could die. In his angelic form he would be immortal; he had to come after the seed of Abraham, David, and Joseph, from sperm, so that he could taste death for every Israelite man.

note.label: Psalm 8: The Son of Man Made a Little Lower Than the Angels

precepts.why:
David says of the son of man, “thou hast put all things under his feet”. Paul shows how that came to be. “But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept. For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.” Christ was made lower than the angels so he could die, and he rose as the firstfruits.

“But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming. Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power. For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet. The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death.”

“For he hath put all things under his feet.” God has put all things under Christ's feet, subjecting the whole earth and the spiritual realm to the Son. That is the dominion David saw, the son of man crowned with glory and honour. “But when he saith all things are put under him, it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him”: the Father who put all things under Christ is not himself under him.

precepts.text: When all is subdued to Christ, the Son himself will be subject to the Father, that God may be all in all.
precepts.point: Christ had to be made lower than the angels so that he could die. In his angelic form he would be immortal; he had to come after the seed of Abraham, David, and Joseph, from sperm, so that he could taste death for every Israelite man.

note.label: Psalm 8: The Son of Man Made a Little Lower Than the Angels

precepts.why:
All things are put under the feet of the son of man, but Paul shows where it ends: “And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all.”

When all is subdued to Christ, the Son himself will be subject unto the Father, that God may be all in all. The dominion given to the son of man in Psalm 8 is real dominion over the works of God's hands, but the Father stands above the Son, and the kingdom is handed back to him.

precepts.text: I die daily; a man must die daily and offend less in the things he is dealing with.
precepts.point: Lord, I have hoped for Thy salvation, and done Thy commandments. My soul hath kept Thy testimonies, and I love them exceedingly. I have kept Thy precepts and Thy testimonies, for all my ways are before Thee.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
Paul says “I die daily.” A man must die daily and offend less in the things he is dealing with. Sometimes we do get offended, but that is part of our pilgrimage, and dying daily is how we come to the great peace of them that love the law, whom nothing shall offend.

That is the same walk David describes: “Lord, I have hoped for thy salvation, and done thy commandments.”

precepts.text: The sting of death is sin; and the strength of sin is the law.
precepts.point: Peter walked with him and was not yet converted. What converts a man is named in the psalm, and what he strengthens his brethren with is the same thing.

note.label: Luke 22: The Passover, the Betrayal, and the Denial

precepts.why:
“The sting of death is sin; and the strength of sin is the law.” Sin is what stings a man to death, and it is the law that gives sin its strength, because the law is what makes it sin. The law is the standard, and the psalm says that same law is perfect, converting the soul.

What converts Peter, and what he strengthens his brethren with when Satan comes to sift them, is the law of the Lord.

precepts.text: He was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve, then of above five hundred brethren at once, then of James, then of all the apostles, and last of all of Paul, as one born out of due time.
precepts.point: Within that time he was seen by many. Cephas is another name for Peter and means stone.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
After his passion Christ “shewed himself alive after his passion by many infallible proofs, being seen of them forty days.” He did not appear for only a day or two; he stayed forty days, speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of the Most High, to open their understanding further.

Within that time he was seen by many: “he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep. After that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles.” Cephas is another name for Peter, and it means stone.

“And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.” Paul was the last to see him. Those are the many infallible proofs: Christ alive, seen by hundreds of witnesses.

precepts.text: Christ was seen of Cephas, the twelve, above five hundred brethren, James, and all the apostles, and last of all he was seen of Paul, years after the resurrection.
precepts.point: Saul arose from the earth, and when his eyes were opened he saw no man, so they led him by the hand into Damascus. He was struck blind by what he witnessed.

note.label: Acts 9: A Chosen Vessel

precepts.why:
Saul was struck blind by what he witnessed. Paul counts what he saw among the appearances of the risen Christ: “he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once”, then “he was seen of James; then of all the apostles. And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.”

Christ was seen of Cephas, the twelve, above five hundred brethren, James and all the apostles, and last of all he was seen of Paul, years after the resurrection. That is what happened on the road: Saul saw the risen Christ, and when his eyes were opened he saw no man, so they led him by the hand into Damascus.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why: He is the first begotten of the dead, and the apostle Paul addressed the same thing concerning Christ: “But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.” Letting you know he was the first to rise from the dead.

points: As we have borne the image of the earthy: we are mortal; Adam lost his immortality. We shall also bear the image of the heavenly: that is a promise from God. He is going to change our cellular structure and give us a new body, no longer this weak, frail body that has to die.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

points: Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God; neither doth corruption inherit incorruption. What we are in now is corruption, and the Lord is going to change this nervous system.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

points: Behold, I shew you a mystery: we shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump. The dead shall be raised incorruptible: no more trauma, no more weak nervous system constantly breaking down. This corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

points: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners. Bitterness spreads like leaven through words: the yeast makes the thing rise, and the angry influence spreads to others through words and attitude.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: Hard times create warriors against sinful impulses. Men are the vanguards of righteousness, to ward off any semblance of sin: see evil going on, blab it out, no X-files up in here, put it on blast so you are afraid to bring nastiness in, because we want blessings from the Lord and not problems. Our people hate change and are afraid of revolutionary thought, as Bishop Nathanyel taught in The Fear of Being Born Again, so everyone who comes in gets tried and watched, and if you refuse to change you have to go; we cannot let a bad example destroy the flock. God would have all come to repentance, 2 Peter 3:9, and we expect you to arrive with negative impulses, but the demons get exercised out of you by the congregation, and you will thank your brothers and sisters for the wounds of a friend rather than the kisses of an enemy.

Proving means a man and a woman working out their differences until they are on one accord about rebuilding the nation, with the man's mind together because he is who she will follow when trouble hits and step in to handle the business. Both must hate sin, fervently, having seen what it did to the generations before, or you end up with the children in that grocery store. Proving is not betrothal; it is seeing if you are compatible, and betrothal is when you are engaged to be married. There is no fornication in proving, and no ceremony over fornication; Malachi 2:16-17 answers the negro laws used to beguile sisters who do not study.

Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners. Evil communications come to men and women, and when they come you shut them down and do not entertain them, as the captain was drilling, or you end up caught in foolishness. A father who came up through this will make sure his sons learn that discipline and are not given feminine softness, so that when he grows up he can deal with a woman properly. That is not abuse.
